newsitem.title: USA: NBC wins Nov 17 weekly ratings - NIELSEN.
newsitem.headline: NBC wins Nov 17 weekly ratings - NIELSEN.

text.p: NBC won the highest ratings for the week ending November 17, attracting nearly 11.5 million households and 17.2 million viewers.

Nielsen's ratings measure the number of households watching a network and are based on all 97 million U.S. households with television sets. Nielsen's share figures also measure households viewership, but are based only on the number of households with their televisions in use.
Each household rating point equals 970,000 households, according to Nielsen.
The unit of General Electric Co was watched by 11.8 percent of all U.S. households with televisions during the average minute that week, according to Nielsen Media Research.
CBS, owned by Westinghouse Electric Co, came in with the second highest ratings, followed by Walt Disney's ABC, Nielsen said.
Fox, owned by News Corp Ltd, placed fourth.
-- NBC drew a rating of 11.8 and a 19 percent share.
-- CBS had a rating of 10.7 and a 17 percent share.
-- ABC had a rating of 9.6 percent and a 15 percent share.
-- Fox had a rating of 6.9 percent and an 11 percent share.
-- UPN, a unit of Chris-Craft Industries Inc and allied with Viacom Inc, had a rating of 3.7 percent and a 6 percent share.
-- WB, owned by Time Warner Inc and Tribune Co, had a rating of 2.8 percent and a 4 percent share.
